title: AI Medical Device Certification Body Scarlet Raises $50M Series B
key_facts: Scarlet closed a $50 million Series B led by Headline; existing investors Kindred Capital, Creandum, Atomico and Entrepreneurs First returned and Notion Capital joined; total funding is about $75 million.
Scarlet was co-founded in London in 2021 by chief executive James Dewar and chief technology officer Jamie Cox, who both previously worked on AI medical devices at Babylon Health.
It is designated a Notified Body under the EU Medical Device Regulation (NB 3022) and an Approved Body under the UK MHRA (AB 8536) and issued its first EU MDR certificate in June 2024.
Scarlet says its customers have cut a year or more from certification timelines for new AI-enabled devices and shortened product-update cycles from months to weeks (company claim).
The money will fund its team of experts and expand its footprint in the US and Asia-Pacific.
Wowtale says the FDA authorised 91 AI/ML-enabled devices in 2022 and 295 in 2025.
Competitors named: BSI, TUV SUD and DEKRA (traditional Notified Bodies) and consultancies such as Hardian Health, Noze and Lindus Health.
